questions.prompt: What basic claim does Chapter 15 make about religion?
choices: It is only about private belief
It can bond groups, display loyalty, and enforce norms as well as express belief
It has no sincere-belief dimension at all

explanation.gentle: The chapter widens religion beyond inward conviction alone.
explanation.direct: Its main move is to treat religion as belief plus group-bonding and loyalty-display practice.
explanation.competitive: Religion can do faith work and group work together.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter highlight group bonding in religion?
choices: Because shared ritual and coordinated practice can create real cohesion
Because religion matters only when private belief disappears
Because bonding has nothing to do with visible practice

explanation.gentle: The chapter says shared practice can help people feel united.
explanation.direct: Bonding matters because coordinated ritual can strengthen group identity.
explanation.competitive: "Ritual synchrony" can help weld a group together.

questions.prompt: Why do sacrifice and ritual synchrony matter in this chapter's model of religion?
choices: Because they can make commitment visible and help bond participants
Because they automatically prove every belief claim true
Because only sacrifice matters and symbols do not

explanation.gentle: Visible cost and coordinated action can show commitment and create solidarity.
explanation.direct: Sacrifice and synchrony matter because they help display allegiance and strengthen cohesion.
explanation.competitive: The cost signals loyalty and the rhythm binds the room.

questions.prompt: A group values a repeated public ritual partly because it shows who is truly committed. Which chapter idea is most visible?
choices: Religion can use visible practice to display loyalty
Religion is only private reflection
Visible commitment eliminates the need for belief

explanation.gentle: The ritual is helping commitment become visible.
explanation.direct: The group is using costly, public practice as a readable signal of allegiance.
explanation.competitive: The act is marking who is really in.

questions.prompt: Why might a student fellowship room use badges, repeated messages, and symbols so heavily?
choices: Because public markers can help enforce norms and belonging expectations
Because symbols matter only when sincere belief is gone
Because religion cannot shape behavior in group settings

explanation.gentle: The chapter says public cues can help keep group expectations visible.
explanation.direct: Badges and messages matter because they support norm enforcement and identity together.
explanation.competitive: The symbols keep the code and the membership signal alive.

choices: Religion can include sincere belief
Visible loyalty signals and norm enforcement can matter in religion
If loyalty signaling is present, religion must be pure manipulation

explanation.gentle: The chapter keeps faith alive while widening religion's social role.
explanation.direct: It rejects the false choice between sincere belief and visible group functions.
explanation.competitive: Signal value does not erase conviction.

questions.prompt: How does Chapter 15 grow out of Chapter 14 on medicine?
choices: It moves from visible sacrifice signaling care to visible sacrifice signaling group loyalty and norm commitment
It abandons visible signaling and focuses only on doctrine
It treats medicine and religion as unrelated

explanation.gentle: After medicine, the book turns to another domain where visible sacrifice matters.
explanation.direct: Religion continues the mixed-motive story by shifting from care signals to loyalty and norm signals.
explanation.competitive: The visible investment moves from treatment concern to group allegiance.

questions.prompt: Why might a visible badge or symbol matter so much in a religious setting?
choices: Because it can make belonging and alignment publicly legible
Because symbols replace every need for shared practice
Because only private belief counts in group life

explanation.gentle: The visible marker can show who belongs and who is aligned.
explanation.direct: Public symbols matter because they help make commitment and membership readable.
explanation.competitive: The badge turns hidden allegiance into a visible signal.

questions.prompt: Why does the chapter insist that religion can express sincere belief while also bonding groups and enforcing norms?
choices: Because faith, visible commitment, and social coordination can coexist in one religious life
Because bonding disappears whenever belief is sincere
Because religion is only about control

explanation.gentle: The chapter's hardest lesson is coexistence, not replacement.
explanation.direct: Religion can retain sincere meaning while also functioning as a loyalty and norm system.
explanation.competitive: Devotion, bonding, and control can stack.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest bridge from Chapter 15 into Chapter 16 on politics?
choices: If religion uses visible practice to signal loyalty and reinforce norms, politics may also use emotion, sacrifice, and participation to signal group allegiance
Politics matters only when religion vanishes
Religion and politics are unrelated in the book's argument

explanation.gentle: The next chapter asks how group loyalty stays visible in civic life.
explanation.direct: Politics extends the loyalty story into democratic participation, strong emotion, and low-information side-taking.
explanation.competitive: After ritual marks allegiance, civic action marks allegiance too.
